title: Money Returned Into a Closing Benefit Period on a Healthy Options Card
content:
Money that came back onto a Ridgecrest Healthy Options Card and was placed in the benefit period being closed is counted into that period, and which kind of returned money is counted depends on what the period holds.

The money counted back into that period is the total of the retailer's own refunds posted into it, where the period carries such a refund; the total of the credits put on the card for a purchase the member questioned, where the period carries no retailer's refund but carries such a credit; and nothing in every other case.

**How the two kinds are told apart.** A retailer's own refund is money the retailer sent back for a returned item, posted into the benefit period the purchase belonged to. A credit put on the card for a purchase the member questioned is money the plan put back on its own finding. Both stand on the card's record as money returned, and each carries the reason it was posted.

| What the closing period holds | What is counted back into the period |
|---|---|
| at least one retailer's own refund | the total of those retailer refunds |
| no retailer's refund, but at least one credit for a questioned purchase | the total of those credits |
| neither | nothing |

**Worked through on hypothetical entries.** A closing period holding a retailer's refund of 19.99 USD and a credit for a questioned purchase of 40.00 USD: a retailer's refund stands, so 19.99 USD is counted back and the credit is not. The same period holding the 40.00 USD credit alone: no retailer's refund stands, so 40.00 USD is counted back. A period holding neither: nothing is counted back.
